key_insight: Jointly selecting anomalous samples and explanatory features under fixed budgets is more robust than feature-first ranking because it avoids calibration-error amplification and preserves sample-feature coupling.
engineering_relevance: Coupling-Grouped XY-QAOA offers a hardware-aware, constraint-preserving QAOA design that cuts circuit cost while scaling to larger feasible bipartite-selection runs on IBM Heron hardware.
method: Formulate anomaly-and-feature choice as a joint fixed-budget optimization problem.
Use Coupling-Grouped XY-QAOA with grouped angles and an XY constraint-preserving mixer.
Apply warm starts and near-budget repair to improve feasible solution quality under hardware limits.
evidence_signal: On matched sparse IBM Heron R3 benchmarks, the implementation reduced depth by 45.9%-61.3% and two-qubit gates by 2.6%-5.2%, with 64-qubit p=2 and 36-qubit p=3 feasible-sector executions and 20-qubit p=5 runs retaining 63% valid samples.
watch_item: Performance is benchmark-dependent and still sensitive to noise, feasible-sector retention, and the quality of warm starts or repair heuristics.
paper_title: Coupling-Grouped XY-QAOA for Joint Anomaly-Feature Selection
